definition: Temporary cookies that are automatically deleted when you close your web browser, used to maintain your login status and preferences during a single browsing session.
metaDescription: Learn about session cookies - temporary files that keep you logged in and remember your preferences while browsing, deleted when you close your browser.
simpleExplanation: Session cookies are like temporary name tags that websites give your browser. They remember who you are and what you're doing while you visit a site, but disappear completely when you close your browser window.
whyItMatters: Session cookies are generally privacy-friendly because they don't persist after you close your browser. However, they can still track your activity during a browsing session and may contain sensitive information like login credentials.
technicalDetail: Session cookies have no expiration date set and exist only in temporary memory. They use the browser's session ID to maintain state between HTTP requests. When the browser closes, the session ends and these cookies are automatically purged from memory, making them less persistent than stored cookies.

examples.explanation: When you log into your bank account, a session cookie keeps you authenticated as you navigate between checking, savings, and bill pay pages. It's deleted when you close the browser for security.

An e-commerce site uses session cookies to remember what items you've added to your cart as you browse different product pages, but the cart empties if you close your browser without completing the purchase.
A news website remembers your language preference or font size selection during your visit through session cookies, but you'll need to set these preferences again on your next visit.
